ph_ping.text: Check the compute is powered on
steps: Look for two solid PWR A/B LEDs.
If no lights appear, long-press the power button for five seconds to power the compute down.
Wait until the LEDs are slow-blinking green, then short-press to power the compute back on.
Try to ping the car again.
ph_ping.source: Dev Ops Troubleshooting Guide v2.2 (Oct 21, 2026), Powering on Vehicle/Compute/RSI/NUC

ph_temp.text: Is it too hot or too cold out?
ph_temp.help: If the outside temperature is too hot or too cold, the compute may not turn on.
ph_temp.source: Dev Ops Troubleshooting Guide v2.2 (Oct 21, 2026), Powering on Vehicle/Compute/RSI/NUC

steps: Keep the vehicle running with the heat on in the cabin.
Turn the rear HVAC to 3/4 heat.
Long-press the power button (5 seconds) to return the LEDs to slow-blinking green.
Short-press the power button to turn the compute on.
If the LEDs go back to solid red (this can take up to 15 minutes), go back to step 3.
When the LEDs go solid green and the compute powers on, return the rear HVAC to cool and carry on.
ph_warm.source: Dev Ops Troubleshooting Guide v2.2 (Oct 21, 2026), Powering on Vehicle/Compute/RSI/NUC

ph_static.text: Set the USB ethernet connection to WIRED STATIC
steps: On the RSI laptop, check the USB ethernet connection.
Make sure it's set to WIRED STATIC, not WIRED DHCP.
Check the connection to the stack again.
ph_static.source: Dev & Bring-Up BOLOs (reviewed 11/6/2026), RSI Laptop Connection Problems
ph_static.help: Temporary BOLO for Perseus trucks, last reviewed 11/6/2026: the RSI laptop loses its connection to the stack or can't reach any websites. No fix yet.
